highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156 raises Apple deployment minimums while improving rendering, pixel access, and text shaping performance.
highlights_body: WebAssembly packages now include the WebGPU implementation, Android texture rendering follows display refresh, and managed pixel and HarfBuzz operations avoid unnecessary allocations.

breaking.title: Apple deployment minimums increased
breaking.body: iOS and tvOS applications must now target version 14.0 or later, and macOS applications must target version 11.0 or later. Update your application deployment targets before adopting this release.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows display refresh
bullets.detail: Synchronizes GL texture rendering with the display refresh cycle to provide smoother Android rendering.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered streams no longer retain their source
bullets.detail: Releases the underlying stream when front-buffered managed streams are disposed, preventing unnecessary retention.

bullets.lead: Image pixel copies reduce managed overhead
bullets.detail: Optimizes managed image pixel copying to reduce work when transferring image data.

bullets.lead: HarfBuzz text processing avoids temporary allocations
bullets.detail: Pools UTF-32 encoding buffers and avoids native feature-string allocations while preserving text shaping and feature decoding behavior.
Ships emdawnwebgpu's implementation inside the native SkiaSharp library so WebAssembly consumers receive the required WebGPU code with the package.
Native assets and managed target metadata now align with iOS and tvOS 14.0 and macOS 11.0.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Packaged the WebGPU implementation with the WebAssembly native library
contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Stabilized Blazor CPU sample tests by waiting for the first canvas paint
